title: Finite-level pro-etale compact-support base change
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be finite, let $\square$ be a
compact-support
base-change square with $f$ separated of finite type and
$g:Y'\to Y$ arbitrary, and let
$K\in D^+(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ carry an
etale-origin witness
$(L,\alpha)$. Then the pro-etale exchange map

$$
g^{-1}Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'_!g'^{-1}K
$$

of [def-cbc-exchange-map] (with the compact-support functors
and exchange map of [def-cbc-exchange-map] transported to the
pro-etale site) is an isomorphism; it is independent of replacing
the witness by an isomorphic one.

Here $\Lambda$ is the finite commutative coefficient ring of [def-cbc-exchange-map], and the small pro-etale categories use constant discrete modules [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For arbitrary bases, the compact-support functors and exchange are the Zariski-local extension [lem-cbc-etale-local-compact-support-extension] of that definition's compactification formulas, transported to etale-origin objects. This supplies their meaning when there is no chosen global compactification; no compactification datum or quasi-compact-open hypothesis is imposed on the square. The witness is that of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. The square and its morphism hypotheses use [def-cbc-compact-support-square] and [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

proof.text: Retain the original unrestricted $f$ and $g$. Put $A_T=\nu_T^*$. The witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] gives $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and $\alpha:A_XL\simeq K$. The morphism $f′$ is separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], so the extension lemma applies to both vertical maps. Use [lem-cbc-etale-local-compact-support-extension] to form the global etale compact-support functors $H_f,H_{f'}$ and the specified natural arrow $E_L:g_e^{-1}H_fL\to H_{f'}g_e'{}^{-1}L$. This supplies the construction missing from the source's initial global choice; it asserts no invertibility. Its restriction to $V'=g^{-1}V$, for any open $V\subseteq Y$, is the arrow for $f_V:X\times_YV\to V$, computed with a compactification of $f_V$ whenever one is available. In steps 2--5 fix an affine open $V\subseteq Y$, work on this restricted square, and abbreviate $f_V,g|_{V'}$ and $L|_{X\times_YV}$ by $f,g,L$. There is no assertion that $V'$ is affine or qcqs.

source.place: Proof, opening choice: explicit local-extension repair without a new hypothesis

proof.text: An affine $V$ is qcqs: apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] to its identity, whose quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness follow directly from the identity diagonal and identity inverse images. The base-change theorem [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], applied to $V\hookrightarrow Y$, makes $f_V$ separated of finite type. Therefore [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies a compactification $c=(j,p)$ over this $V$. The open immersion $j$ is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target], applied to $X_V\xrightarrow{j}\overline X_V\xrightarrow{p}V$: $X_V\to V$ is finite type and $p$ is separated because it is proper. Thus quasi-compactness is proved, not assumed. [def-cbc-compact-support-square] supplies $c'=(j',p')$ over arbitrary $V'=g^{-1}V$. By the properness convention [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], proper $p,p'$ are quasi-compact by finite type and quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], so both meet the direct-image comparison hypotheses.

source.place: Proof, opening choice: Nagata applied only to affine target charts

proof.text: The local witness representative $L$ is bounded below; restriction and inverse image are exact for constant module coefficients as in [def-cbc-exchange-map]. The hypotheses of [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] now hold on this chart: finite commutative $\Lambda$, separated finite-type $f$, compactification with quasi-compact open part proved in step 2, and arbitrary $g:V'\to V$. Hence the compactification exchange $E_L^c$ is an isomorphism and is natural in $L$. By the localization and normalization clauses of [lem-cbc-etale-local-compact-support-extension], this is precisely the restriction of the global etale arrow of step 1. It is not necessary to choose a global compactification of the original $f$.

source.place: Proof, etale finite-torsion theorem, applied chartwise

proof.text:
Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$. Exactness of $A_T$ is [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]. Etale extension by zero preserves quasi-isomorphisms and acts degreewise by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], and pro-etale extension by zero is exact and degreewise by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. For a representative complex $C$ of $L$, apply the natural sheaf comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] in each degree. Naturality with respect to $d_C^n$ says the resulting components commute with the differentials; their inverses do too. This gives a chain isomorphism $e_{j,L}:A_{\bar X}j_!^eL\simeq j_!^pA_XL$, independent of the representative, since all functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. In particular $j_!^eL$ stays bounded below. Take $b_p$ to be the specified canonical counit-mate direct-image comparison normalized in [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange], not an arbitrary choice of isomorphism; its underlying natural isomorphism is [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]. Combine it with $e_j$ to obtain
$$C_{c,L}:A_Y Rf_!^{c,e}L=A_YRp_*^ej_!^eL\xrightarrow{b_{p,j_!L}}Rp_*^pA_{\bar X}j_!^eL\xrightarrow{Rp_*^p(e_{j,L})}Rf_!^{c,p}A_XL.$$
Both arrows are isomorphisms, natural in $L$. For $M=g_e'{}^{-1}L$, the base-changed formula is explicitly
$$C_{c',M}:A_{Y'}Rp'_*^ej'_!^eM\xrightarrow{b_{p',j'_!M}}Rp'_*^pA_{\bar X'}j'_!^eM\xrightarrow{Rp'_*^p(e_{j',M})}Rp'_*^pj'_!^pA_{X'}M.$$
Here $M$ is bounded below because etale inverse image is exact, as in [def-cbc-exchange-map]; the degreewise natural comparison for $j'$ gives $e_{j',M}$ and the qcqs map $p'$ gives $b_{p'}$.

source.place: Proof, local proper/open comparisons, chain-level extension made explicit

proof.text:
Let $a_u:A_Uu_e^{-1}\simeq u_p^{-1}A_V$ be the natural pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. With $C_c$ from step 4 define
$$S_L=g_p^{-1}(C_{c,L})\circ a_{g,Rf_!^{c,e}L},\qquad T_L=Rf'_!^{c',p}(a_{g',L})\circ C_{c',g_e'{}^{-1}L}.$$
Thus $S_L$ has source $A_{Y'}g_e^{-1}Rf_!^{c,e}L$ and target $g_p^{-1}Rf_!^{c,p}A_XL$, while $T_L$ has source $A_{Y'}Rf'_!^{c',e}g_e'{}^{-1}L$ and target $Rf'_!^{c',p}g_p'{}^{-1}A_XL$. They are natural isomorphisms. By the transported-map convention in the original statement, the transported compact-support exchange is explicitly
$$F_L=T_L\circ A_{Y'}(E_L)\circ S_L^{-1}.$$
This is the transport of the composite defining [def-cbc-exchange-map], rather than a choice of an arbitrary isomorphism between its endpoints. For its proper part [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange], applied to $p,p'$ and $j_!^eL$, identifies the conjugated proper exchange with the specified pro-etale proper exchange. For its open part [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] supplies the canonical pro-etale extension-by-zero base-change isomorphism on complexes. We only need the transported composite specified in the item, so no claim about a separately normalized compact-support transformation outside the etale-origin class is used.

source.place: Proof, local conjugation identifies the transported compactification formula

proof.text: Return to the original global square and its etale arrow $E_L$ of step 1. Every geometric point of $Y'$ lies in $g^{-1}V$ for some affine open $V\subseteq Y$. By step 3 the restriction of $E_L$ there is an isomorphism. Exact inverse image commutes with kernels and cokernels, hence with cohomology, by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Thus every $\mathcal H^q(E_L)$ is an isomorphism at every geometric stalk. [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes each underlying abelian-sheaf map an isomorphism; its inverse is $\Lambda$-linear because $\mathcal H^q(E_L)$ is, so it is also an isomorphism of module sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] to the abelian category of constant $\Lambda$-module sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]: since every cohomology map is invertible, $E_L$ is an isomorphism in its bounded-below derived category. This uses local detection for an already constructed global morphism; it does not infer gluing of arbitrary morphisms in the ordinary derived category.

source.place: Proof, missing passage from local compactification models to arbitrary bases

proof.text:
Use the transported functors meant in the original statement. Explicitly, on etale-origin objects one may take $F_f=A_YH_fR\nu_{X,*}$ and $F_{f'}=A_{Y'}H_{f'}R\nu_{X',*}$. The unit isomorphism $\eta_T:\operatorname{id}\simeq R\nu_{T,*}A_T$ of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] gives natural comparison isomorphisms $C_{f,L}=A_YH_f(\eta_{X,L}):A_YH_fL\simeq F_fA_XL$, and similarly for $f'$. Pullback preserves etale origin by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], so all these formulas are defined. On an affine compactification chart, let $q^f_c:H_f\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!^{c,e}$ be the comparison from step 1 and define $D_{c,L}=C_{c,L}\circ A_Y(q^f_{c,L})\circ C_{f,L}^{-1}:F_fA_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!^{c,p}A_XL$. Define $D_{c′,M}$ by the displayed formula of step 4 with $M=g_e′{}^{-1}L$. For a restriction of a global object, insert $r^f_V$ and the pullback comparison $a$ first; their compatibility with $q$ is part of the extension node. The equation $D_{c,L}C_{f,L}=C_{c,L}A_Y(q^f_{c,L})$, and its primed equation, show that conjugating the formula below by these endpoint identifications cancels $C_f$ and $C_{f′}$ and gives exactly the compactification formula of step 5: the middle arrow becomes $E^c_L$ by the normalization in step 3, and naturality of $a_{g′}$ moves it past the target comparison. Thus this is also the transported map of the source on every compactification chart. With $a_u$ the pullback comparison set
$$S_L=g_p^{-1}(C_{f,L})\circ a_{g,H_fL},\qquad T_L=F_{f'}(a_{g',L})\circ C_{f',g_e'{}^{-1}L}.$$
Their sources are $A_{Y'}g_e^{-1}H_fL$ and $A_{Y'}H_{f'}g_e'{}^{-1}L$, respectively, and their targets are $g_p^{-1}F_fA_XL$ and $F_{f'}g_p'{}^{-1}A_XL$. The global transported arrow on $A_XL$ is therefore
$$F_L=T_L\circ A_{Y'}(E_L)\circ S_L^{-1}.$$
All its factors are invertible by step 6 and the displayed comparisons. Put $P=g_p^{-1}F_f$, $Q=F_{f'}g_p'{}^{-1}$; the actual map on $K$ is $Q(\alpha)\circ F_L\circ P(\alpha)^{-1}$ and is invertible. For another witness $(L',\alpha')$, full faithfulness in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] lifts $\alpha'^{-1}\alpha:A_XL\to A_XL'$ uniquely to $u:L\to L'$. Lifting the inverse and using faithfulness shows that $u$ is invertible. Naturality gives $F_{L'}P(A_Xu)=Q(A_Xu)F_L$. Substitution of $\alpha'A_Xu=\alpha$ into the two witness formulas and cancellation proves equality of the actual arrows on $K$. No global compactification, qcqs base, residue-characteristic restriction, or constructibility hypothesis was used.

split_report.summary: Repair of E1 and 7b: restored the exact upstream assertion with unrestricted f and g; removed the supplied-compactification and quasi-compact-open hypotheses. Read the actual blueprint and Stacks/SGA sources in the launcher literature directory. Added one statement-only construction/localization interface for the etale compact-support functor and arrow over arbitrary bases. Apply Nagata and finite-torsion base change only on affine target charts, derive quasi-compactness of each open part, detect the global etale isomorphism by cohomology stalks, and transport with explicit conjugation and witness cancellation. The new node asserts existence/local formulas, not base-change invertibility. Second reading replaces undefined enhancement/uniqueness language by explicit ordinary-category interface equations, cites base-change stability for both vertical maps, and uses the existing cohomology-isomorphism criterion directly.
split_report.blueprint: Opening sentence 'Choose a compactification': repaired at proof steps 1--2 by Zariski-local construction plus local Nagata. Finite-torsion comparison: step 3. Proper and open site comparisons: steps 4--5. Globalization absent from the source: step 6. Transport and independence of witness: step 7. The unit's coefficient-stage route is retained; no unit/chapter file is changed.
split_report.statement_dispute: STATEMENT-DISPUTED (construction/type defect, not a counterexample to base change): def-cbc-exchange-map only supplies compactification-dependent formulas, while the exact source allows arbitrary bases and its proof invokes a global compactification without justification. Correct the construction by its explicit Zariski-local extension; do not add hypotheses. The upstream assertion is retained verbatim before this clarification.
